[h1]简介[/h1] 这是一款俄罗斯方块游戏，但加入了肉鸽的要素，可以说是一款“小丑方块”也不为过，《连爆方块》很好的将俄罗斯方块与肉鸽要素相结合，为俄罗斯方块这种有几十年玩法的游戏注入了好玩和更随机的要素，玩法还是在限定的回合数内，消除方块的行数，获得要求的分数就能过关。但关卡也做成了肉鸽的爬塔方式，每个关卡都可以获得一些带有效果的方块，这些方块虽然还是常规的方块外形，但附带的效果就就非常有意思了，比如带有爆炸效果的，消除的时候除了消除本层的方块数，还可以消除额外带爆炸的方块，爆炸可以连携爆炸，所有带爆炸的都可以被消除掉，非常的有趣。完成几个关卡会受到一个随机的“减益”提高游戏的难度，比如反向操作，原本往下落的方块变成往天上飘，还有快速下落的，方块出现后只有几秒的思考和调整时间，时间一到就会马上落下等等。当然高风险带着高回报，在本身的俄罗斯方块框架下的分数奖励，在带上肉鸽的玩法，达到目标要求的分数还是挺简单的，而且这个过程还会受一些随机的影响带来一些额外的快乐。 [h1]总结[/h1] 总的来说，这款《连爆方块》肯定受到不少“小丑牌”的影响，肉鸽要素对俄罗斯的方块影响的非常全面，虽然看着还是俄罗斯方块，但实际上手游玩却是不一样的感觉，构筑好准备玩的build，在不同方块的效果和特性下打出爆炸的分数。 [quote]欢迎关注我们的鉴赏家:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402982/]走心评测[/url] ←遵从内心，写出真实感受 欢迎加入我们Steam组:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/ZXPC]走心评测[/url]←点击加入，一起探索游戏的乐趣 喜欢这篇评论，也麻烦点个赞，让更多人能够看到！[/quote]

For the Tetris side of things- as a somewhat decent modern tetris player (U rank on TETR.IO and 10k+ on TE:C) I can tell that the developer also plays modern Tetris; the completely customizable controls, 180 spin, SRS, 7 bag, adjustable handling even! The game feels buttery smooth to play. The only thing I noticed was that the pieces spawn 1 tile to the right of where they usually do in other Tetris games, which messed with my muscle memory a little bit but it's a very minor thing I can overlook when the rest of it plays this well. The bosses are mostly interesting and challenging, with the upside-down one (the Defiant) being the most difficult for me as it's the one that deviates from the standard Tetris I'm comfortable with. The Thief and The Perfectionist are trivially easy for players like myself due to the way you're kind of railroaded into playing the game (I'll talk more about that later). As for the Roguelike side of things, it is a perfectly functional and enjoyable experience. For me, I'm not really thinking about the specific types of blocks as I'm placing them, I'm simply 9-0 stacking them like how I would in regular Tetris games, but that seems like how the game converges as you approach the higher levels. That brings me back to the previous point; the game seems to railroad you into playing a certain way. The abilities of all the blocks and perks all seem to encourage simply stacking a single well as high as you can, then clearing an I piece to collect all of the multiplier bonuses. I feel like there is so much more potential to encourage different playstyles, such as incorporating spin bonuses, combo-based bonuses, back to back bonuses, etc. Here are a few suggestions I feel would give the game much more player expression; - Perk that gives Stack if the line clear is a spin - Perk that gives an increasing multiplier of Flow the more 4-line clears you do in a row (e.g. the first Quad clear gives 1x flow, second gives 2x flow, etc. and resets when you don't clear a quad) - Perk that gives you back some blocks when you perform an All Clear - Block that slightly reduces the score requirement when you perform a spin using it (unrelated suggestion that I think would be cool) - A high-level boss that makes blocks invisible after x blocks have been placed after them All in all, a very solid game and the developer should be very proud of what they've created. Personally, I've actually been waiting for someone to make a Tetris-based roguelike and I'm very impressed with this one, considering how well it plays. I hope the developer takes all the feedback from the community in account to create an incredible game.

[h2] 游戏介绍 [/h2] 《爆连方块》是Caue Ferrareto制作的一款以经典游戏俄罗斯方块为基础玩法的策略肉鸽游戏，在保留原版随机下落方块消除玩法的同时，又融入了肉鸽元素，玩家带来独一无二的全新消除体验。 [h2] 玩法介绍 [/h2] 万物皆可肉鸽，从扑克牌到麻将，肉鸽元素的融入让很多经典游戏焕发了新生机，本作也不例外，经典游戏俄罗斯方块（Tetris）的玩法相比大部分人都知道，不规则的方块从上方随机掉落，玩家通过移动、旋转摆放这些几何块体，使其形成完整的横向排列并消除得分，这也是本作的基础玩法，以消除和得分为主要目标。 说实话本作的画面有些像《小丑牌》，都是像素风的界面。与前者一样，本作也是打破了传统游戏玩法的框架进行了创新，游戏中包含了肉鸽爬塔要素，不同于原版俄罗斯方块之时图形的不同，本作中玩家每关都能得到一些带特殊效果的方块，利用特殊效果玩家可以得到更高的分数，只要达到目标分数即可过关。 就像原版俄罗斯方块掉落速度越来越快，缩短玩家的思考时间，本作的提高难度的方式就显得天马行空了，不仅有快速下落，还有会往上面去的，以及突然下落等等，但这也增加了游戏关卡的不确定性和刺激性，让玩家对于接下来碰到的方块有了更多的期待。 [h2] 总结 [/h2] 总的来说这款游戏算是对俄罗斯方块进行了比较成功的肉鸽创新，既保留了原版的玩法，使得玩家上手容易，又加入了肉鸽随机元素，增强了游戏的策略性，推荐给喜欢类似于《小丑牌》等游戏的玩家尝试入手。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

Feels too inconsistent and RNG-heavy. After a certain point, the only way to survive the insane point requirements is to have an essentially perfectly crafted deck, but with only 5 rerolls it's almost impossible to get a good enough deck. Most of my runs die before level 10, and it feels like just a grindfest to get through the trivially easy early levels just to hit a brick wall once the point requirement climbs beyond what you can realistically get from a single 4-line clear / tetris combo. Half the blocks and perks are even actively bad to add to your deck, because they either come with punishing downsides (not being able to hold a piece anymore? really?) or will actively ruin your board state when they trigger, turning your clean stack into a hole-riddled nightmare. If I wanted to play tetris, I think I'd rather just play normal tetris, without these insane scoring requirements and clunky boss mechanics (simply reversing your controls does not make for engaging gameplay..); and if I wanted a roguelike deckbuilder, there's about 1000 games on Steam with more engaging mechanics than this.

If you are not VERY GOOD at Tetris, this one is probably worth a skip. And that's 95% of the reason for the thumbs-down. I really like the mechanics, but very frequently find myself making a single mistake and that results in losing the level, often because I just simply run out of pieces, even if every placement after the mistake is perfect: I recover, but end up just not having enough pieces left. And I've gone from scoring 9,000,000 points on a level to scoring a measly 50,000 (with a goal of 100,000) on the next just due to draw order, too. I think my best game was getting to Level 18. Other times it'll be picking up a new block to add to my draw pile and its special quirk ends up thrashing my score (here's looking at you Crystal Block). Other times it's the every-third-level "boss" level where it decides that it's going to be a jerk and mess with you (screw you, Puppeteer, screw you--instantly dropped a block in the orientation I wanted it on the same frame its effect triggered and the piece dropped into place...rotated). Definitely some quality mechanics here, but the tuning is just [i]really[/i] tight. And that's on [i]welcome to the game[/i] difficulty! I honestly have no idea what the other difficulty/deck options even [i]are[/i] (or for that matter, how many levels it takes to win a run).

It’s a very basic idea: “what if Tetris was a deckbuilding roguelike?” The premise alone is taking three mechanical concepts, all of which have kinda been done to death by this point, and then smashing them together in a way that one hopes would make the result feel like more than the sum of its parts. The problem, simply put, is that while it does work, it doesn’t work well enough to be called “fun.” All of the block types seem like they add more problems than solutions, the scoring system scales out of hand for all but a few reliably good block types that one should ideally always specialize in, and the boss stage “challenges” are depressingly unimaginative. This isn’t a bad game, it’s just a boring game, born of trying to be a carbon copy of very specific things that other games have done a far better job of being. It feels lifeless and uninspired, and every “huh, this seems interesting” moment is soon undercut by the realization that it only sounded interesting in theory, or in the case of a golden few, was so easy to lean on that it basically becomes a guaranteed win condition to be aimed for at all times. Play it if you want to, it has heart. It definitely tries. It’s not a bad game in the slightest. But don’t expect much from it, either. Because the sad truth is, if you’re looking for a Tetris clone, a deckbuilder or a roguelike, there’s far better alternatives on all three fronts.

[h1][b]新式花式爆炸俄罗斯方块[/b][/h1] [h1]游戏介绍[/h1] 俄罗斯方块相信没有人没玩过吧，不过爆炸类的俄罗斯方块还是比较少见的。本作有点Boomliss的影子，不过玩法上有更多的创新元素。 [h1]玩法与游戏性[/h1] 本作的玩法是以经典俄罗斯方块为基础，用各种功能的方块来达到各种特殊效果以通过超过关卡的目标分数来破关。前期难度小，后期目标分数陡增，这一点不是很友好。每三关都会有BOSS关卡，即随机带一个Debuff，通过BOSS关卡后会给予一个相当不错的增益。每解锁一种方块，都会在方块百科里呈现。当然并不是所有方块都是有增益性的，玩家需要与之前获得的方块来互相搭配来取得收益最大化，有些方块甚至是坑方块，所以还要权衡利弊。另外本作还有多人模式，不过也就是共享排行榜而已。 [h1]设计与特点[/h1] 本作最大的特点是在设计上有很多种方块。爆炸类、海盗类、蜜蜂类、和弦类、辐射类、矿物类、赌狗类等类型的方块各有特点和响应的属性，玩家通过每一关结束获得随机选择的类型方块来在接下来的关卡中组合以达到最大的分数。在各种类型的方块设计上，脑洞大开，给玩家游玩途中的多样性体验不错，基本不会有游玩疲劳。在分数设计上，本作还需要平衡，前期很简单，后期突然分数很多，而且如果后期BOSS如果是城堡的话，基本可以说完蛋了。另外一个比较致命的平衡就是方块太少，其实可以参考FC和SFC上的BPS的俄罗斯方块2炸弹版，基本每一关都是99个方块，这样就没那么快速破关或者快速失败了，希望之后制作组会在这方面有所改进。 [h1]画面与音乐[/h1] 像素画风很不错，颜色搭配充足，带有动感的音乐恰到好处，而且复合本游戏的题材。视觉效果上趋于普通，也没有特别炫丽的烧眼场景，很是不错。另外音效也和特定方块搭配一起，非常丝滑。 [h1]综合体验[/h1] 作为一款休闲的小游戏还是很不错的，如果喜欢俄罗斯方块的玩家当然是很推荐游玩这款游戏了。 [quote] 我的游戏真的有那么好玩吗? 关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/34823631/]“我的游戏不可能那么好玩！”鉴赏家[/url],这是你从未体验过的船新版本~ [/quote]

Along the infinite quest to add Balatro's format to different proven games, Stackflow gleefully reaches Tetris and to great success. 1.0 is much improved from the Demo I played a long time ago, and I can see myself coming back to this game for a long time. Stackflow isn't as in-depth or varied as Balatro, you will see most of what the game has to offer fairly quickly, but in that smaller pool it is much easier to find your breaking points consistently and trying new combos is quick and easy. I also really like the "multiplayer" mode, which really just amounts to daily and weekly leaderboards. But it's fun to see others play around alongside you day in and day out. It also comes with some good advanced settings to finetune the Tetris part of the game to how you like to play, so you'll feel right at home! If you want a different flavor of Tetris, Stackflow is a strong option.

After playing a couple dozen runs from Early Access to full release and having half of them wrenched away from me due to something beyond my control - from not getting crucial pieces in time to getting frame-perfected by The Puppet Master and screwing my run - I think I'm done. Far too much of your success comes down to RNG in such a way that your actual skill and ability to pull a build together stops mattering; many pieces rely on being played early, and only a handful of them scale well into the endgame. You can be as clever as you want putting together pieces from contrasting themes and getting something out of it, if a crucial "scaling" piece like the Queen Bee or Reactor doesn't arrive in time, you're doomed. And the less said about the several pieces that can transform [i]other[/i] pieces on the board (especially those who do it at complete random, like Mimic and Bookshelf), the better. The economy system was a great addition and alleviates a lot of the frustration I had with earlier versions when it comes to [i]attaining[/i] the pieces you want or need, but even the best runs can be shot down because the game didn't feel like giving you an I-Block when fighting The Perfectionist. And pivoting your build is a joke, you can only remove pieces from your deck with a single perk unless you feel like giving up the ability to Hold pieces... which breaks the game in its own right. That's not to say that StackFlow's take on "Tetris but Balatro" is any kind of bad idea; there are many builds that can give you the same hit of dopamine by means of block-retrigger spam sending your score into the stratosphere, but that doesn't imply your build is viable for any stage past 20 where point targets suddenly accelerate into multiple millions. Some of the bosses are fun; The Warden works the best, I'd say. But so many of them are obnoxious and frustrating, disrupting the flow of the game at best (such as The Defiant, The Mirror) or making it a chore to play outright (The Oracle, The Thief, [i][b]The Puppet Master[/b][/i]). And some of the piece effects are fairly imaginative and fun to use, especially as you complete sets of related blocks and watch them all interact. I just wish the game surrounding it was more enjoyable than haplessly frustrating.

After about 20 minutes of playing I saw all this game had to offer. None of the block types do anything particularly interesting. Even the current sale price of $5.24 as of this review is a steep ask for the amount of gameplay this game provides.

I've been playing Tetris for as long as Ive been able to hold a controller. I have thusfar thoroughly enjoyed the time that I've spent on this Stackflow, and I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed Balatro or Gambonanza, and also enjoys Tetris. Notably, as of the time of this review, the game has only been out for a few days, and this is very apparent in the balance of the blocks available. Some of the "classes" (I can't think of what else to call them) do NOT have very good synergy with other blocks in the same class. As it stands, building into any particular class feels like it doesn't have the potential to reach the last level. They seem to plateau quite hard beyond a certain point. The sole exception that I've seen has been the Casino class ("Let's go gambling!"). The gambling blocks scale to an abosolutely wild extent since they multiple based on your current level. In my opinion, I think the rest of the blocks need to be scaled up in a similar fashion, to some extent, so that it becomes possible to reach the final levels when focusing on any specific class. Alternatively, having bonuses for using blocks in the same class, beyond just the block effects, could help.

An interesting idea that made for a fun game (while I was blissfully unaware)... ...Which I unfortunately have to give a negative review on principle, because the game's code was written with the assistance of generative AI. My proof being, the latest update post links to a GitHub repository for in-development Workshop support, which lists Anthropic's Claude as a contributor. Looking at the commits, the example mod is AI assisted, and so are some changes made to the readme. You could technically argue that this only proves that Workshop support is AI assisted, not necessarily the game itself; but it'd be foolish to have any hope when [b]updating a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ readme[/b] was too hard for the "dev". Regardless of how you feel about generative AI, there's no excuse for not at least disclosing this when Steam literally gives you a space on the store page specifically for it. Unfortunately, what Steam does [b]not[/b] provide is a way for users to actually report undisclosed pre-generated assets (which does include code, before anyone asks), and it's been too long for me to try refunding it. Best I can do now is post this review, and hope no one else has to get blindsided like I did.
